findings.claim: FY2025 net revenue was USD 32.8bn, up 16%, with operating margin of 57.6% against 55.3% in 2024. Q4 2025 revenue grew 18% and EPS 25% on strong cross-border volume.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Q2 2026 net revenue was USD 9.3bn, up 14%, with adjusted earnings of USD 5.04 per share against a USD 4.77 consensus. Growth was driven by cross-border volume, switched transactions and value-added services.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Mastercard Q2 2026 results; Zacks via Yahoo Finance

findings.claim: Value-added services and solutions produced USD 3.8bn of Q2 2026 net revenue, up 20% — roughly 41% of the total and growing appreciably faster than the payment network itself.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to low-teens net revenue growth on a currency-neutral basis excluding acquisitions, from a previous range of high-end-of-low-double-digits to low-teens, citing stronger first-half performance.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE

findings.claim: FY2026 net revenue is estimated at approximately USD 37bn, applying low-teens growth to the FY2025 base of USD 32.8bn.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: FY2026 adjusted earnings per share are estimated at approximately USD 19.75, from Q2 actual of USD 5.04 and a full year growing in the mid-teens.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from reported quarterly EPS and the guided growth rate

findings.claim: Growth is margin-accretive and has been for years: operating margin expanded 230 basis points in FY2025 while revenue grew 16%. This is the cleanest example in this series of growth that expands returns rather than diluting them.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Unusually for this protocol, almost none of the valuation rests on speculative demand. The business is priced on cash flows it is already generating, which is the opposite of the Apple, Alphabet and SpaceX dossiers.

conclusions: The operating performance is outstanding and unusually clean: FY2025 revenue up 16% to USD 32.8bn with operating margin expanding 230 basis points to 57.6%, and Q2 2026 revenue up 14% with an EPS beat.

Value-added services are now roughly 41% of revenue and growing at 20%, faster than the network. That is both a genuine diversification away from pure interchange and a partial answer to the substitution threat.
Growth is margin-accretive — the cleanest example of it in this series. Mastercard expands returns as it grows rather than diluting them.
Almost none of the valuation rests on speculative demand, which is the opposite of the Apple, Alphabet and SpaceX dossiers. The business is priced on cash flows it already generates.

The corresponding weakness: revenue is recurring by behaviour, not by contract, and there is no backlog. The risk is not that promised demand fails to arrive — it is that existing demand migrates to another rail.
thesisImpact: Phase 3 establishes that this is a rare case where the base case needs almost no speculative content. That has a direct consequence for Phase 5: the valuation can be built on demonstrated cash flows, which makes the discounted cash flow the most trustworthy instrument here rather than the least — the reverse of every other company in this series.
